# ntfsck

> Read-only-first NTFS consistency checker and repairer for Linux.

## Overview

ntfsck inspects an NTFS volume through a hexagonally-architected Go codebase: a
pure on-disk decoder (`internal/ntfs`), a small core that resolves the `$mft`
extent and checks metadata consistency (`internal/volume`, `internal/check`,
`internal/repair`, `internal/report`), and adapters for a real device and for
in-memory test fixtures. It diagnoses and plans repairs but does not yet apply
them.

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fabianoflorentino/ntfsck.git
cd ntfsck
make build
bin/ntfsck --check /dev/sdb1
```

## Key Concepts

- **$mft extent**: resolved from MFT record 0's non-resident `$DATA` runlist, not
  from the boot sector's `$mft` zone cluster.
- **Ports at the consumer**: `volume.Source`, `check.Volume`, and `repair.Volume`
  are declared where they are used, not beside their implementations.
- **Read-only first**: `--check` opens read-only; `--repair` prints a plan and
  writes nothing.
- **NotCovered is separate**: structures a build does not examine never affect the
  consistency verdict.

## CLI

- `ntfsck --check [--output text|json] <device>`
- `ntfsck --repair [--dry-run] <device>`
- `ntfsck --dump-mft [--mft-record N] <device>`

Exit codes: `0` OK, `1` failure, `2` usage, `3` inconsistent.

## Core Types

- `ntfs.BootSector` / `ntfs.RecordHeader` / `ntfs.Attribute` — decoded on-disk
  structures.
- `ntfs.Run` — one decoded runlist entry; `ntfs.ClusterAt`, `ntfs.ClusterCount`.
- `volume.Volume` — an open volume with `MFTRecordBytes`, `RecordCount`, `ReadAt`.
- `check.Report`, `check.Finding`, `check.Severity` — the check outcome.
- `repair.Plan`, `repair.Action` — an ordered set of intended writes.
- `report.Format` — `text` or `json`.

## Error Handling

- `ntfs.ErrNotNTFS`, `ntfs.ErrBadRecordMagic`, `ntfs.ErrAttributeNotFound`,
  `ntfs.ErrNoRuns`
- `volume.ErrRecordOutOfRange`, `volume.ErrNoMFTExtent`
- `check.ErrUnreadableStructure`
- `repair.ErrNothingToRepair`, `repair.ErrNotImplemented`
- `device.ErrReadOnly`

Match with `errors.Is`.
